correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=2 with N=2^m, both endpoint skew-tent branches reduce by exact floor/ceiling algebra to reversal and cyclic shift. The parity hybrids have explicit parity-preserving affine reflections as second iterates, implying fourth powers equal identity. The two congruences 2z=0 (mod N) and 2z=-2 (mod N) have solutions of the specified parity, giving exactly four two-period points for C_1 and none for C_{N-1}. The full two-/four-cycle counts follow by exhaustion; the zeta functions follow from primitive-cycle factors. The m=2 exceptional order of C_1 is explicitly included. Packaged pure-Python exact-integer checks confirm all advertised identities and counts for m=2..14 and 65,528 endpoint/state pairs, but the proof does not rely on extrapolating those checks.

originality.rationale: The source defines the exact parity-selected hybrid and proves bijectivity and a discrete Lyapunov exponent law, but its Sections 4-5 treat period behavior empirically and explicitly identify systematic cycle-length analysis as unfinished. Bijection alone has no implication for order four. The pure shift S_{N-1} has order N even though the hybrid C_{N-1} has order four; general dLE claims likewise do not identify primitive-cycle counts. value.rationale: The source specifically calls for systematic analysis of raw periodic orbit lengths as a prerequisite for understanding its finite-precision map behavior. Two natural admissible endpoint parameters admit a complete, nontrivial and strongly contrasting classification at arbitrary precision. The endpoint hybrid at a=N-1 reduces the underlying full cyclic shift of length N to a permutation of exponent four; all raw outputs are therefore limited to four symbols even as N grows and the source's dLE estimate approaches its maximum. Exact cycle counts, fixed-point spectra and dynamical zeta functions follow from the same structural proof, rather than disconnected routine parameter exercises. This gives a direct mathematical boundary on using the discrete Lyapunov diagnostic alone to infer desirable periods. It does not claim cryptographic insecurity of all postprocessed generators or describe generic controls.
